real: Stocks have slid since their early September peak
anon: Shares have slid for a month since hitting a record
note: Dow peaked Sept 3, 1929 (Fed History). Day 1 of the run is a month into the slide.

real: After the close, Fisher sees stocks on a high plateau
anon: After the close, an expert says shares are not too dear
note: Remark made in a speech on Oct 15 and printed in the New York Times on Oct 16 (Fed History cites NYT p. 8); placed on the day it appeared. Adjudication: speech on the evening of 15 Oct, reported in the NYT of 16 Oct.

real: Panic selling; bankers meet at Morgan to prop up stocks
anon: Frantic selling grips the market before a late recovery
note: Time, 4 Nov 1929: noon meeting at 23 Wall St (Lamont, Mitchell, Potter, Wiggin, Prosser); Richard Whitney bid for U.S. Steel about 1:30 pm. File close is down 3.2% because the afternoon recovery cut the day's losses; line does not state a move.

real: Hoover says the nation's business is on a sound basis
anon: Leaders insist the economy is in good shape
note: Statement issued Oct 25 in reply to press questions; wording of the line is our paraphrase. Confirm page text.

real: Black Monday: stocks suffer their worst fall yet
anon: Shares plunge as the panic comes back
note: Fed History: Dow fell nearly 13% on Oct 28. In the file this is the biggest fall of the run so far.

real: Black Tuesday: panic selling again, stocks plunge
anon: Selling floods the market for a second day
note: Fed History: Dow fell nearly 12% on Oct 29.

real: Stocks leap back as Rockefeller says he is buying
anon: Shares bounce back as wealthy buyers step in
note: John D. Rockefeller (Sr.) statement that he and his son had for some days been buying sound common stocks; press dated it Oct 30. The Time 1970 page quotes it without a date, so the date needs a second source. File: biggest one-day rise of the run so far.

real: New York Fed cuts its lending rate from 6% to 5%
anon: The central bank makes borrowing cheaper
note: Fed Bulletin Dec 1929: reduced from 6 to 5 per cent effective Nov 1. Announced on Oct 31 (NY Fed circular dated Oct 31), exchange shut on Nov 1.

real: New York Fed cuts its lending rate again, to 4.5%
anon: Borrowing gets cheaper again
note: Fed Bulletin Dec 1929: cut from 5 to 4.5 per cent effective Nov 15. Newspapers dated the announcement Nov 14; second source should confirm.

real: Hoover gathers industry chiefs to hold wages and jobs
anon: The president meets business leaders to protect jobs
note: Nov 21 morning meeting with industry leaders, afternoon with labour. URL taken from a search snippet; confirm it is the Nov 21 White House statement.

real: After the close, Hoover says the worst has passed
anon: After the close, the president sounds upbeat
note: Chamber of Commerce dinner speech on the evening of May 1, after the close, so placed on May 2. Adjudication: speech at 9:30pm on Thu 1 May.

real: Over the weekend, Congress passes Smoot-Hawley tariffs
anon: Over the weekend, lawmakers back higher taxes on imports
note: Senate passed it Fri June 13 (44-42); House final vote Sat June 14 (check); Hoover signed June 17.

real: Caldwell's main bank in Tennessee closes
anon: A big regional banking group's lead bank closes
note: Fed History: Bank of Tennessee (Nashville), a main Caldwell and Company subsidiary, closed Nov 7, 1930.

real: The Bank of United States fails in New York
anon: A big city lender shuts and locks its savers out
note: Fed History: ceased operations Dec 11, 1930; fourth-largest bank in New York City. Closed that morning by the state banking superintendent.

real: Over the weekend, Hoover proposes a pause on war debts
anon: Over the weekend, the president offers relief on debts
note: Announced after Hoover's news conference on the evening of Sat June 20, statement embargoed to June 21 (American Presidency Project). Proposes a one-year postponement of intergovernmental debts.

real: Britain abandons the gold standard
anon: A big trading partner lets its currency fall
note: Fed History dates Britain's departure from gold to Sept 21, 1931.

real: Hoover signs the Reconstruction Finance Corporation Act
anon: A new government lender is set up to help firms
note: Signed Jan 22, 1932 (Fed History).

real: Over the weekend, Hoover signs the Banking Act of 1932
anon: Over the weekend, a law lets the central bank lend more
note: Signing date taken from memory and the essay header (Feb 27, a Saturday); the Fed page gives no exact day, so check against the Statutes at Large.

real: After Friday's close, the Senate rejects the war bonus
anon: After the close, lawmakers vote down a payout
note: Senate defeated it on Fri June 17, 1932 (62 to 18, per the Capitol Visitor Center) after debate ran into the evening; next trading day is Mon June 20.

real: A new law lets the RFC lend to states and cities
anon: Lawmakers let the rescue lender help states and cities
note: Fed History: on July 21, 1932 an amendment authorised the RFC to lend to state and local governments (Emergency Relief and Construction Act).

real: Nevada declares the first state bank holiday
anon: A state shuts its banks to stop a rush for cash
note: Fed History: Nevada first, Oct 31, 1932; Michigan followed Feb 14, 1933.

real: Michigan shuts every bank with a bank holiday
anon: Another state closes its banks to stop a run
note: Fed History: Michigan declared a banking holiday on Feb 14, 1933.

real: After the bank holiday, the stock exchange reopens
anon: Share trading resumes after a long pause
note: Roosevelt's bank holiday began Mon Mar 6; the NYSE stayed shut until Wed Mar 15 (check the exact closure in an NYSE source).

real: Roosevelt signs the Banking Act, insuring deposits
anon: A new law aims to make bank savings safer
note: Banking Act of 1933 (Glass-Steagall), signed June 16, 1933; set up the FDIC.

real: Roosevelt signs the law creating the SEC
anon: A new law brings tighter rules for share dealing
note: Securities Exchange Act of 1934, 48 Stat. 881, approved June 6, 1934.

real: Germany invades Poland and war breaks out in Europe
anon: A country is invaded and war breaks out abroad
note: Invasion began early on Sept 1, 1939 (Roosevelt's bedside note, 3:05 am).

real: After the Pearl Harbor attack, the US enters the war
anon: The nation enters a world war
note: Attack on Sun Dec 7; Roosevelt addressed Congress at 12:30 pm on Dec 8 and war was declared that day.

real: Over the weekend, North Korea invades South Korea
anon: Over the weekend, a country is invaded by its neighbour
note: Invasion began June 25, 1950 (Sunday in Korea, Saturday night in the US).

real: Overnight, an armistice halts the fighting in Korea
anon: Overnight, a truce halts a war
note: Signed on the morning of July 27, 1953, Korean time, which is the evening of July 26 in New York.
